text: Because B sits on its own branch: a wire runs from Battery + to Lamp B left, and another from Lamp B right back to Battery −, so that loop is still complete. Removing Lamp A only opened the gap between A's own sockets. Can you trace B’s complete path while avoiding A’s empty socket?

No. Lamps transfer electrical energy into light and heat; they don't use up current. Both lamps are dark because Lamp A is removed, leaving an open gap between its sockets, so the loop from Battery + back to Battery − is broken. Where did removing A break the shared path?
